arxiv-2003-02060.creator: L. Wu ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, D.O. Kharchenko ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, V.O. Kharchenko ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, O.B. Lysenko ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, V. Kupriienko ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, S. Kokhan ? {}^{\textsf{\footn
arxiv-2003-02060.description: Abstract A generalized model to study dislocation loops growth in irradiated binary Zr-based alloys is presented. It takes into account temperature effects, efficiencies of loops to absorb point defects dependent on the loop size, an influence of locality of grain boundary sink strength, and concentration of the alloying element.

arxiv-2102-06363.title: New Distributed Source Encryption Framework
arxiv-2102-06363.creator: Yasutada Oohama and Bagus Santoso
arxiv-2102-06363.description: Abstract We pose and investigate the distributed secure source coding based on the common key cryptosystem. This cryptosystem includes the secrecy amplification problem for distributed encrypted sources with correlated keys using post-encryption-compression, which was posed investigated by Santoso and Oohama.

arxiv-2311-02871.title: Channel Attention for Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2311-02871.creator: Gekko Budiutama, Shunsuke Daimon, Hirofumi Nishi, Ryui Kaneko, Tomi Ohtsuki, Yu-ichiro Matsushita
arxiv-2311-02871.description: Abstract Quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) have gathered attention as one of the most promising algorithms for quantum machine learning. Reduction in the cost of training as well as improvement in performance is required for practical implementation of these models.

arxiv-2403-11381.title: Can LLM-Augmented autonomous agents cooperate?, An evaluation of their cooperative capabilities through Melting Pot Journal: Artificial Intelligence Journal
arxiv-2403-11381.creator: Manuel Mosquera, Juan Sebastian Pinzón, Yesid Fonseca, Manuel Ríos, Nicanor Quijano, Luis Felipe Giraldo, Rubén Manrique
arxiv-2403-11381.description: Abstract As the field of AI continues to evolve, a significant dimension of this progression is the development of Large Language Models (LLMs) and their potential to enhance multi-agent artificial intelligence systems. This paper explores the cooperative capabilities of Large Language Model-augmented Autonomous Agents (LAAs) using the well-known Melting Pot environments along with reference models such as GPT-4 and GPT-3.5.

arxiv-2406-14703.title: Do LLMs Have Distinct and Consistent Personality? TRAIT : Personality Testset designed for LLMs with Psychometrics
arxiv-2406-14703.creator: Seungbeen Lee Seungwon Lim, Seungju Han, Giyeong Oh, Hyungjoo Chae, Jiwan Chung, Minju Kim, Beong-woo Kwak, Yeonsoo Lee, Dongha Lee, Jinyoung Yeo, Youngjae Yu, Department of Artificial Intelligence, Yonsei University Department of Computer Science, Yonsei University, Department of Electrical and Com
arxiv-2406-14703.description: Abstract Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to their adaptation in various domains as conversational agents. We wonder: can personality tests be applied to these agents to analyze their behavior, similar to humans? We introduce TRAIT , a new benchmark consisting of 8K multi-choice questions designed to assess the personality of LLMs.

arxiv-2503-11032.title: Weakly Supervised Contrastive Adversarial Training for Learning Robust Features from Semi-supervised Data
arxiv-2503-11032.creator: Lilin Zhang, Chengpei Wu, Ning Yang
arxiv-2503-11032.description: Abstract Existing adversarial training (AT) methods often suffer from incomplete perturbation, meaning that not all non-robust features are perturbed when generating adversarial examples (AEs). This results in residual correlations between non-robust features and labels, leading to suboptimal learning of robust features.

pmc-10507979.title: LncRNA SLCO4A1-AS1 suppresses lung cancer progression by sequestering the TOX4-NTSR1 signaling axis
pmc-10507979.creator: Yi-Ling Chen, Yi-Nan Liu, Yen-Ting Lin, Meng-Feng Tsai, Shang-Gin Wu, Tzu-Hua Chang, Chia-Lang Hsu, Huey-Dong Wu, Jin-Yuan Shih
pmc-10507979.description: BackgroundMetastasis is a multistep process involving the migration and invasion of cancer cells and is a hallmark of cancer malignancy. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play critical roles in the regulation of metastasis. This study aims to elucidate the role of the lncRNA solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 4A1-antisense 1 (SLCO4A1-AS1) in metastasis and its underlying regulatory mechanisms.

pmc-11643834.title: Enhancing Photoelectrocatalytic Efficiency of BiVO4 Photoanodes by Crystal Orientation Control
pmc-11643834.creator: Hongru Zhao, Xinkong Wei, Yue Pei, Weihua Han, Francis Leonard Deepak
pmc-11643834.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bismuth Vanadate (BiVO4) is a promising photoanode material due to its stability and suitable bandgap, making it effective for visible light absorption. However, its photoelectrocatalytic efficiency is often limited by the poor transport dynamics of photogenerated carriers. Recent research found that varying the atomic arrangement in crystals and Fermi levels across different crystal orientations can lead to significant differences in carrier mobility, charge recombination rates, and overall performance.

pmc-11728852.description: Babesia canis is the parasite responsible for a life-threatening disease for dogs in Central Europe, of which the main vector is the ornate dog tick—Dermacentor reticulatus. The objective of the presented study was to assess the prevalence of Babesia infection in dogs with clinical suspicion of babesiosis, which tested positive for B.

pmc-12617199.title: PL005. Child Safety Across Settings: Protecting Children from Violence and Injuries
pmc-12617199.creator: Mark Bellis, Shanthi Ameratunga, Alyson Pollock, Koen Maertens, Mamta Shah
pmc-12617199.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Children across Europe continue to face a dual burden of unintentional injuries from road traffic crashes, drowning, burns, falls, poisonings, leisure and sport, as well as intentional harms, including violence, neglect, and bullying. While child injury mortality has declined in several domains, injuries remain one of the leading causes of premature death and disability in young people and stark inequalities exist within and across countries. Unintentional injuries rank among the top causes of child mortality in Europe.

pmc-12619733.title: Effects of small extracellular vesicles isolated from pleural effusion on lung cancer cell proliferation and migration
pmc-12619733.creator: G. Cammarata, A. Masucci, I. Giusti, V. Dolo, C. Di Sano, S. Taverna, E. Pace
pmc-12619733.description: Pleural effusion (PE) is a common clinical manifestation associated with advanced stages of both malignant and non-malignant diseases. PE frequently occurs in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and contributes to tumor progression. NSCLC accounts for more than 85% of the lung cancers and remains a problem worldwide due to its late diagnosis and low rate of response to treatment.

pmc-12651221.title: Clarifying the Dual Role of Staphylococcus spp. in Cheese Production
pmc-12651221.creator: Alessandra Casagrande Ribeiro, Déborah Tavares Alves, Gabriela Zampieri Campos, Talita Gomes da Costa, Bernadette Dora Gombossy de Melo Franco, Felipe Alves de Almeida, Uelinton Manoel Pinto, Javier Carballo, Juan Antonio Centeno
pmc-12651221.description: Staphylococcus spp. present a dual role in cheese production as some species are pathogenic, while others bring beneficial characteristics. Coagulase-positive staphylococci (CoPS), particularly Staphylococcus aureus, are of concern due to their ability to produce enterotoxins linked to foodborne outbreaks. These toxins, encoded by staphylococcal enterotoxin (SE) genes, cause gastroenteritis, especially vomiting.

pmc-13258278.title: Rural–Urban Differences in Hypertension Prevalence and Control in a Large Regional Health System Cohort
pmc-13258278.creator: Yordanos M. Tiruneh, Susan McBride, Huaxin Song, Matthew Decaro, Alaa Rihan, Theresa Byrd, Alex Baham, Jared W. Magnani, Elmer V. Bernstam, Jarett D. Berry
pmc-13258278.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Rural US populations bear a high burden of cardiovascular disease, with hypertension contributing to the rural–urban gap. We examined hypertension prevalence and control across the rural–urban continuum among patients in a large healthcare system in Northeast Texas. Methods: We analyzed the electronic health record data from 363,539 patients with at least one outpatient encounter between September 2021 and April 2025. We defined hypertension using ICD-10-CM codes, antihypertensive prescriptions, or a blood pressure ≥ 130/80 mm Hg.

pmc-13450100.title: The Evolving Landscape of Gout in the Female: A Narrative Review
pmc-13450100.creator: Jennifer Lee, Nicholas Sumpter, Tony R Merriman, Ru Liu-Bryan, Robert Terkeltaub
pmc-13450100.description: Gout is at least three times more prevalent in males than in females. However, concurrent with rising total gout prevalence, complex factors, including comorbidities, diet, lifestyle, and aging, have promoted higher gout prevalence in females. This narrative review focuses on summarizing recent developments in the landscape of gout in females and the mechanisms involved.

pmc-13453408.title: Retrospective Analysis of Adverse Drug Reactions in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Development of a Risk Prediction Model
pmc-13453408.creator: Bo Sun, Qian Guan, Qin Zhou
pmc-13453408.description: BackgroundPatients with diabetes are prone to adverse drug reactions (ADRs) during long-term medication, but the related risk factors and predictive models remain to be clarified.ObjectiveTo analyze the influencing factors of ADRs in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and to develop and validate a risk prediction model.MethodsClinical data of 254 randomly selected patients with T2DM were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-13526227.title: When Silence Masks Autism: Delayed Autism Diagnosis in an Adolescent With Deafness
pmc-13526227.creator: Stephanie E King, Erika Ryst, Nikhat Kaura
pmc-13526227.description: A 13‐year‐old adolescent male was referred for an interdisciplinary autism assessment. His complex medical history included a traumatic delivery (with drop in heartrate and nuchal cord), neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, diagnosis of profound congenital hearing loss, diminished bile ducts on liver biopsy at 1 month of age, and a seizure disorder.
